body.p: I. Introduction

The undersigned thanks Examiner Yankey for review and consideration of the present Application. In response to the Office Action of April 3, 2024 ("Office Action"), the undersigned submits the present amendment and remarks ("Response").

Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 1, 4, 5, 8-16, and 19-22 will be pending in this application. Claims 1 and 8 have been amended, claims 6, and 7 18 have been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer, and new claims 19-22 have been added. Support for amendments can be found at least in FIG. 3 of the published application. No new matter is added. Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims.
AFCP 2.0 Request:

Furthermore, it is respectfully submitted that this Amendment should be considered and entered under the Patent Office's "After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0" (AFCP 2.0) because the contents of the response herein may lead to allowance of the application with only limited further search and/or consideration. Applicant's representative is willing and available to participate in any interview requested by the examiner concerning the present response. II. Drawing Objections

The drawings are objected as the subject matter in claims 6 and 7 is allegedly not illustrated. Without acknowledging the propriety of the objection and solely to expediate prosecution, claims 6 and 7 are cancelled, rendering the drawing objections moot. III. Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. & 112

Claims 6-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly feature related to the wall in claim 6 was unclear. Without acknowledging the propriety of the rejections and solely to expediate prosecution, claims 6 and 7 are cancelled, rendering the § 112 rejections moot.
IV. Claim Reijections under 35 U.S.C. " 102 & 103
Claims 1 and 4-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 10,501,188 B2 to Nicholas et al. ("Nicholas"). Claims 1 and 4-10 are rejected

under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2013/0241247 Al to Wallace et al. ("Wallace"). Claims 11 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas. Claims 11 and 13 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of Wallace, as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,794,902 B2 to Pothier ("Pothier"). Claims 11-12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of Pothier. Claims 11-12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of Wallace in view of Pothier, as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2013/0126671 Al to Guering ("Guering"). Claims 14-16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas. Claims 14-16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Nicholas in view of Wallace, as applied to claim 1 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2017/0283064 Al to Robinson ("Robinson"). Applicant traverses this rejection and requests its withdrawal.
Independent claim 1 has been amended solely to expedite prosecution of this case. Claim
1, as amended, recites inter alia:

Amended claim 1 further clarifies the seat unit structure by introducing the lateral side, and the front edge of the seat pan and their relative positioning with respect to an access path and a console. Applicant notes that, these first and second positions can be achieved in an "upright" seat configuration. Nicolas and Wallace do not appear to teach or suggest these features.

Nicholas describes a seat unit with a table surface curving into the aisle. However, the table surface is not positioned as claimed. For example, the table surface is not spaced apart from the footrest along a longitudinal axis of the aircraft cabin to define an access path between the console and the footrest.

Furthermore, Nicholas discloses a leg rest positioned between the seat pan and foot rest- see annotated Fig. 7c of Nicholas below. Hence, Nicholas does not describe that in the second position of the seat the front edge of the seat pan is arranged contiguously with the footrest such that the footrest and seat pan together form a continuous surface.

Wallace discloses a seat that is movable in the upright sitting configuration. Further, the Examiner in reference to Fig. 3 of Wallace analogizes seat in the second configuration, as the claimed second position in claim 1. However, Fig. 3 of Wallace shows the seat in a lie-flat sleeping configuration, not in an upright sitting configuration (see also para [0030] of Wallace). A lie-flat sleeping configuration cannot reasonably be interpreted as an upright position. Hence, a person of ordinary skill in the art cannot reasonably combine Wallace with Nicholas. There also seem to be good reasons why the seat of Wallace couldn't be directly imported into Nicholas. For example, the seat of Wallace requires a fairly large ottoman 18 to form part of the bed surface. In Nicholas, there is no substantial ottoman (because the leg rest of the seat forms the bed surface). Therefore, the seat of Wallace in the arrangement of Nicholas couldn't be used as a bed. As such, a person of reasonable skill would not make this combination.

the console is positioned between a lateral edge of the seat pan and the aisle and such that the lateral edge of the seat pan is spaced apart from the access path, and in the second position of the seat, the front edge of the seat pan is arranged contiguously with the footrest such that the footrest and seat pan together form a continuous surface and such that the lateral edge of the seat pan is positioned in the access path, between the console and the footrest. Also, the combination cannot result in a seat configuration where a passenger can access the surface formed by the footrest and seat pan from the aisle through the partially exposed side of the footrest and across the lateral edge of the seat pan.

For at least the reasons presented above, Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claim 1 is not rendered obvious by Nicholas or Wallace alone or in combination. Dependent claims are believed allowable at least due to their dependence from the independent claim 1, as well as the features they recite individually. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections be withdrawn and that these claims be allowed.
V. New Claims

Claims 19 to 22 are newly added. Support for these new claims can be found, at least in FIG. 3. No new matter has been added. Applicant submits that claims 19 and 20 are allowable at least for the reason of their dependence upon allowable base claim 1 and for the reason that their additional recitals further distinguish them from the cited references. Independent claims 21 and 22 include subject matter of claims 19 and 20, respectively. For example, independent claim 21 is allowable because none of Nicholas or Wallace can be reasonably modified to describe "the seat pan is spaced apart from the footrest to a second position in which a front edge of the seat pan touches the footrest such that the footrest and seat pan together form a continuous surface." Independent claim 22 is allowable because Nicholas or Wallace cannot be modified to describe "the movable panel is rotatably mounted with respect to the footrest via a hinge."
Favorable consideration of these new claims is respectfully requested.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
